question.leadin: The author of The Thorn Birds, Colleen McCullough, hails from this country.
question.text: Name this country whose literary tradition also includes Patrick White, whose novel Voss depicts Ludwig Leichhardt lost in the outback.
question.clue: This country commemorates abuses committed against its native population on National Sorry Day.

swap.text: This is the collective name given to Aboriginals who were taken from their families and forced to assimilate into white society. In 2008, Prime Minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized to this group.
swap.clue: An official 2007 apology to these people and their descendants was made by then-Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

question.text: This man has hidden in an Ecuadorian embassy since 2012, a saga stemming from sexual assault charges now dropped. His 2010 talk was "Why the World Needs Wikileaks".
question.clue: Daniel Ellsberg praised this man, saying his actions were similar to Ellsberg's handling of the Pentagon Papers.

swap.leadin: These people have had protest tents set up opposite the Old Parliament House since 1972.
swap.text: Name these people, whose children, the "Stolen Generations," were removed from their families.
swap.answerHtml: Aboriginals [or Aborigines; accept, but DO NOT REVEAL, Australian Aboriginals or descriptions of indigenous or native people of Australia]

question.leadin: Answer the following about the failure of the Gallipoli Campaign.
question.text: The date of the Gallipoli landing is a day of remembrance for this expeditionary force, which was composed of soldiers from two British commonwealths.
question.answerHtml: ANZAC [or the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps]
question.clue: Their most notable action is remembered in the song titled "And the Band Played" a certain nationalist folk tune, was supported by the French from Kum Kale, and was advocated by Winston Churchill.

swap.leadin: In order to pass otherwise deadlocked legislation, this party called its country's only-ever joint sitting of Parliament in 1974.
swap.text: Name this party. Australia's 1975 constitutional crisis was caused by John Kerr's dismissal of a Prime Minister of this party, Gough Whitlam, after the Liberal-National Coalition blocked supply to this left-wing party's government.
swap.clue: This political party passed important social reforms under leaders like Bob Hawke and Gough Whitlam.

question.leadin: Identify the following about penal colonies.
question.text: The First Fleet, under the command of Arthur Phillip, established a prison colony in this Australian state. Sydney is located in this present-day state.
question.clue: The Tenterfield Oration, calling for states to unify for purposes of defense, was given in this state, which was also the landing spot for Arthur Phillip and the First Fleet.

swap.leadin: To support his country's involvement in one conflict, this leader stated he was "all the way with LBJ."
swap.text: Name this Australian prime minister who disappeared in 1967 while swimming at Cheviot Beach.
swap.clue: This prime minister declared that he was "all the way with LBJ" in showing his country's support for the Vietnam War.

question.text: The band Midnight Oil wore jackets with "SORRY" on the back to draw attention to the Stolen Generations during the 2000 Summer Olympics in this Australian city. This is the most populous city in Australia.
question.clue: Lachlan Macquarie ("LACK-lan muh-KWAIR-ee") was placed in charge of this city after John Macarthur overthrew governor William Bligh in the Rum Rebellion.

swap.leadin: In 2008, Prime Minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized to the Stolen Generation, who were children of these people that were forcibly taken from their families.
swap.text: Name these indigenous people of Australia.
swap.clue: These victims of the Myall Creek massacre were also targeted in the Black War.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the "White Australia" policy of discrimination.
question.text: This prime minister of Australia during World War Two, a member of the Labour Party, defended the policy by declaring the country "the home of the British race" in a 1942 speech.
question.clue: Later, New Zealand and Australia laid out their post-WWII military and political goals in the Canberra Pact, signed by this Australian prime minister. Frank Forde finished this prime minister's term after his death in office.

swap.text: This bushranger belonged to the Greta mob and a later "gang" named after him. While under siege by the police at Glenrowan, this man wore an iron bulletproof suit.
swap.clue: This man sent a lewd note wrapped around calves' testicles to Jeremiah McCormack's wife.

question.text: A major event in the Aboriginal Rights Movement was the 1985 ceremony that returned ownership of this monolith to the Anangu. A 99-year lease on this enormous monolith has kept the Anangu from forbidding people to climb it.
question.clue: In 2017, Australian Aboriginals and Torres Strait Islanders held a convention at this rock formation in central Australia that is sacred to local tribes.

swap.leadin: A leader of this party named Johannes Strydom was nicknamed "Lion of the North."
swap.text: Identify this party, which first won a majority in parliament in a 1948 election under Daniel Francois Malan's leadership. Its government implemented the Group Areas Act and the Land Acts.
swap.clue: This defunct right-wing party first led by J. B. M. Hertzog, who formed a government after defeating the United Party led by Jan Smuts in 1924.

question.text: This World War II-era Prime Minister of Australia served for a record 18 years. After an electoral defeat, he formed the Liberal Party to provide conservative opposition to the Labor Party.
question.clue: This Liberal politician who also tried to ingratiate himself with ordinary citizens by delivering the 'Forgotten People' Speech. He was succeeded by Harold Holt.

swap.leadin: The death of this state's senator Bertie Milliner allowed its premier to controversially appoint Albert Field, giving the opposition a majority and leading to "The Dismissal" of Prime Minister Gough ("goff") Whitlam.
swap.text: Name this state that was led for almost two decades by "the hillbilly dictator" Joh Bjelke-Petersen ("Joe BYELL-kee Petersen"). Eddie Mabo fought this state in a 1992 court case that struck down the concept of terra nullius.
swap.clue: In a battle named for the capital of this state, troops rioted for two days in November 1942 against Douglas MacArthur and their American allies.

question.text: Lindqvist recounted the mistreatment of Aboriginal Australians in a 2007 book titled for this phrase. This two-word Latin phrase names a legal doctrine used to justify colonization that was rejected by the Mabo case.
question.answerHtml: terra nullius [accept terrae nullius; accept Terra Nullius: A Journey Through No One’s Land]

swap.text: This Australian Labor Party PM's foreign minister Gareth Evans claimed the Santa Cruz massacre was merely an "aberration." This personal friend of Suharto served as PM from 1991 to '96.

question.text: The shootout where Kelly was captured occurred in this small town in Northeast Victoria. A plan to derail train carrying policemen was foiled by the efforts of hostage Thomas Curnow.
question.clue: Kelly was captured in a shootout with police in this town in Victoria.

swap.leadin: Celebrate Australia Day by getting some points on this bonus. FTPE.
swap.text: Australia Day commemorates the day in 1788 when this group of eleven convict-laden ships under the command of Arthur Phillip landed to establish the first European colony on the continent.
swap.clue: This group that arrived in Botany Bay in 1787. This group carried nearly 600 convicts from Portsmouth, England in a 250-day journey.
